experiment_kind: R1 strong fixed-frequency baseline: the existing adaptive controller held at 2.0 Hz, compared with corrected fixed 1.3 Hz and adaptive reference cohorts. This configuration does not declare an executed result.

mpc.control_parameterization: one historical cubic segment, four knots per force, 48 total parameters

failure.description: Native gym_quadruped invalid non-leg/foot ground contact; no added roll/pitch or height cutoff

video.selection: seed 0 and the lowest-index failed and successful table1/adaptive_fixed episodes, if present, replayed continuously through completion or failure without cutting

implementation_choices: Use the pinned modern author code c46cb9a3960554cffc467a71c6674b65c0f4a2c8 with the dated gym-quadruped Aliengo model efb7217b9515613b238405846dcdbc92cf07f488 and the same explicit source patches as r1-foothold-clock-repaired. The new high-fixed-frequency cohort has not yet been executed; neither source snapshot is certified as the exact original paper release.

Retain the historical foothold behaviors already used by r1-foothold-clock-repaired: lateral hip-to-foot offset 0.1 m per side and world-frame lift-off points fixed throughout each swing. Preserve the modern API and all other executed helper choices; do not claim these restore the entire 2024 control chain.

Keep phase_consistent_swing enabled exactly as in r1-foothold-clock-repaired. At a frequency change, the existing implementation scales elapsed swing time by new_period/old_period. This cohort does not repeat the clock-correction experiment.

Use table1/adaptive_fixed, the same adaptive controller implementation, cost, sampling and low-level execution as the corrected reference groups. The runner derives the singleton candidate [2.0] Hz from locomotion.frequency_hz and initializes and resets the gait at that frequency. The inherited candidate_hz list is not used by adaptive_fixed. Only the fixed frequency changes relative to the corrected fixed 1.3 Hz cohort; compare against both that existing cohort and corrected adaptive to distinguish online selection from always using a higher frequency.

Paper omits numerical Q/R/covariance. Use historical sampling Q, sigma, and one-segment cubic interpolation; nominal acados retains its different author Q/R. Compare common physical task metrics rather than treating different optimizer costs as equivalent.

The historical and modern naive samplers use two Gaussians plus a uniform component at fixed scales, retaining the previous mean as a candidate. Preserve the actual author implementation and disclose its difference from the paper description of multiple Gaussian distributions.

Enable the sampling input-force cost specified in the paper, using nominal acados force weights 0.001 and masking nominal stance load on swing legs. Historical and modern sampling source comment out this term; its inclusion is a paper-method reimplementation choice, not literal historical-code reproduction.

Use absolute MPPI lambda=1 without cost-spread normalization. Disable OT-MPC, gradient refinement, Riccati feedback, foothold optimization, integrators, external wrench compensation, reflexes, velocity modulation, and friction compensation.

Use historical SciPy cubic swing, gains 5000/100, step height 0.3*hip_height, velocity averaging, and 5 cm velocity-error correction clipping. Preserve modern CoM-based SRBD state and corresponding base-height reference adjustment; historical source used base position. Modern initial gait phase is fixed rather than the historical random global phase.

Keep the adaptive implementation and actual contact phase input unchanged. Its frequency regularizer retains the existing reference 1.3 Hz; for the singleton fixed 2.0 Hz candidate this adds the same constant to every rollout and does not alter the selected force trajectory. Do not change the regularizer, sampling budget or controller for this comparison.

Paper states 21 kg, while dated and modern author models are approximately 24.638 kg. Use the actual MJCF mass and initial-pose inertia consistently in all controllers. The dated model retains its damping, friction, armature, torque limits, contact options, and home pose; the massless foot-body adapter only supports the modern feet-position API.

The inherited Figure 3 and Figure 4 protocol blocks are reference definitions only and are outside this configuration's execution budget. Execute table1/adaptive_fixed only. The separate isolated Figure 3 comparison uses the existing nominal-frequency configuration.

Retain the declared Table I reconstruction: 60 s, forward command 0.5 m/s, six-axis random wrench within +/-20 N/Nm, 2 s holds beginning at 2 s, and native gym-quadruped invalid-contact termination. Use the same 50 seeds (0 through 49) as r1-foothold-clock-repaired. This is an additional strong-baseline mechanism comparison, not an extra experiment claimed to appear in the original paper. Do not shorten the task or tune the disturbance to match published percentages.

Paper Mean Cost/tracking-error scalar is not fully defined. Retain linear-velocity error norm, RMSE, common quadratic state/input metrics, task duration, and all success/failure outcomes separately. Do not equate lower error on a prematurely terminated episode with better full-task performance.

Separate first-solve JIT compilation from steady-state solve time while retaining it in raw trajectories. Record actual hardware, command, source/configuration versions and new output paths. Reference corrected fixed 1.3 Hz and adaptive trajectories at their original paths; do not relabel them as newly executed high-frequency episodes.

execution_budget.reference_results: r1-foothold-clock-repaired/table1/adaptive_fixed at 1.3 Hz and table1/adaptive with [1.3,2.0,2.4] Hz; retain original trajectory paths and hashes. No existing cohort is rerun by this configuration.
